_comment: Allow rules live in settings.local.json: a project settings.json's allow rules are ignored until the workspace is trusted, which breaks unattended `claude -p --permission-mode dontAsk` runs. Deny rules and hooks below apply regardless of trust, and deny always beats allow. File rules use Edit(...) not Write(...) - Write rules are not evaluated by file permission checks, while Edit rules cover every file-editing tool including Write.
_comment_credentials: The two credential denies are the most important rules in this file. .env holds a Gmail app password and a Canvas token; state/graph-token.json holds a Microsoft refresh token. Both are denied for READ as well as write, because the failure mode is not the agent editing them - it is the agent quoting one into a run report, which is then rendered by the control plane and committed to runs/ forever. There is no legitimate reason for the agent to see either file: run_sweep.ps1's scripts read them, and hand the agent only the classified digest.
_comment_onedrive: There is deliberately no blanket Edit(~/OneDrive/**) deny: this bot's tree lives under OneDrive/Desktop/Agency, so a blanket rule would block it writing its own runs/ and the bot would fail silently every day. The protection is positive instead - guard_writes.py permits ONLY runs/ and state/dryrun/, and denies everything else including this bot's own scripts and settings.
